name: energent
description: Independent audits of AI-produced work: Energent checks numbers and claims against your source files and reports what is wrong.

interface.longDescription:
AI assistants can make mistakes in numbers, formulas and claims. Energent gives ChatGPT a second opinion. Ask ChatGPT to send its work to Energent, and an independent Energent auditor checks it against your source files in its own sandbox. The auditor writes a report that shows which numbers and claims are correct, which are wrong, and what to fix. You read the findings in the same chat, and you can open the full audit in the Energent web app.

Use it to check financial models, reports, reconciliations, summaries and data analyses before you share them. After you fix the errors, ask for a re-audit: the auditor keeps the earlier findings and checks what changed.

Requires an Energent.ai account.
defaultPrompt: Audit this report against the data I attached.
Use Energent to check the numbers in this summary.
I fixed the errors. Ask Energent to check it again.

positive.description: Audit a summary against its source data
positive.prompt:
Use Energent to audit summary.md against bank.csv.

bank.csv:
date,description,amount
2026-07-03,Client payment A,1200
2026-07-18,Client payment B,450
2026-08-05,Client payment C,980
2026-08-22,Client payment D,320
2026-09-09,Client payment E,1100
2026-09-27,Client payment F,630

summary.md:
Total deposits from July to September were $4,780. Deposits grew every month. September was the highest month at $1,730.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts an audit and waits for it. Reports that the total of $4,780 is wrong (correct total: $4,680) and that 'deposits grew every month' is false (August $1,300 is lower than July $1,650). The September figure of $1,730 passes. Gives the link to the audit in the Energent web app.

positive.prompt: Show me the audit report file from that Energent audit.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the files of the latest audit and shows the report (an HTML or Markdown file) or its download link.

positive.prompt: I fixed the summary: "Total deposits from July to September were $4,680. Deposits dipped in August and rose again in September. September was the highest month at $1,730." Ask Energent to check it again.
positive.expected_behavior: Sends the updated summary to the same audit. The re-audit passes all three claims.

positive.prompt: What is the status of my Energent audit?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the audit status (running, needs_input, completed, failed or stopped) and, when completed, the final answer.

positive.prompt:
Use Energent to audit summary.md against bank.csv, then stop the audit right away.

bank.csv:
date,description,amount
2026-07-03,Client payment A,1200
2026-07-18,Client payment B,450
2026-08-05,Client payment C,980
2026-08-22,Client payment D,320
2026-09-09,Client payment E,1100
2026-09-27,Client payment F,630

summary.md:
Total deposits from July to September were $4,780. Deposits grew every month. September was the highest month at $1,730.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts the audit, then stops it and confirms that the audit task was stopped.

negative.description: Sending email is not supported. Energent does not send email or messages, so the app should not call Energent and should tell the user it cannot send email.
negative.prompt: Email the audit results to my manager.

negative.description: Other Energent conversations are not available. The app can only see audits it started, so it should explain that it cannot list the user's other Energent conversations.
negative.prompt: Show me all my other Energent conversations.

negative.description: Unrelated request. A general question with no work to audit should be answered by ChatGPT without calling Energent.
negative.prompt: What is the capital of France?

review.commerce_description: Energent does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT. Audits use the credits of the user's existing Energent plan.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: start an audit, follow it, read the findings and report, answer the auditor, re-audit, and stop an audit.
